chunks: It is his saying (peace be upon him): "The place to proceed to is Paradise, and the place of doom is Hell."

He differentiated between the two words due to the difference in their meanings, and did not say: 'The place to proceed to is Hell,' as he said: 'The place to proceed to is Paradise,' because proceeding (al-istibaq) is only towards something beloved and a desired goal, which is the attribute of Paradise. This meaning is not present in Hell, may we seek refuge in Allah from it! Therefore, it was not proper for him to say: 'And the place to proceed to is Hell,' but he said: 'And the doom is Hell,' because the end (al-ghayah) is reached by one who may or may not be pleased with reaching it, and by one who is pleased with it. Thus, it was suitable to use it to express both matters together.

key_terms.السَّبَقَةُ: The place to proceed to / The one who runs ahead
key_terms.الِاسْتِبَاقَ: Proceeding / Running ahead / Competing to reach
key_terms.الْغَايَةُ: The end / The doom / The final destination

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali use different words for Paradise and Hell in this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the rhetorical precision of using 'al-sabiqah' (the proceeding/racing) for Paradise and 'al-ghayah' (the end/destination) for Hell, noting that racing implies an eager pursuit of a beloved goal, which suits Paradise's allure. In contrast, 'al-ghayah' is a neutral term for a final endpoint, applicable to both those who welcome their fate and those who dread it, thus covering the dual nature of Hell. This linguistic distinction highlights the psychological and spiritual orientation of the believer versus the general outcome of the disbeliever.
